thread: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request
subject: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request — Council-held planning, heritage and public-authority record for Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr, Llandough
body:
Democratic and Scrutiny Services
Vale of Glamorgan Council
Democratic@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk

cc: FoiUnit@valeofglamorgan.gov.uk (for information only — this is not a new FOI request)

Dear Democratic and Scrutiny Services,

Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / request for a focused Task and Finish Review

I am a resident with a long-standing family connection to Great House Farm (Tÿ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth. A public documentary archive of the site is maintained at:

https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/

I request that the Council consider a focused Scrutiny Topic Suggestion leading to a Task and Finish Review (or other appropriate scrutiny mechanism) concerning the Council-held planning, heritage, environmental and public-authority record relating to Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr / Church View Close.

Proposed scope (within the Council’s remit):

• the Council-held planning, heritage, environmental and public-authority record relating to Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr / Church View Close;
• the chronology of Council decisions, records and responses from the mid-twentieth century onwards;
• identification of missing, contradictory or unresolved Council-held records and, where appropriate, referral to the body with the relevant jurisdiction;
• consideration of the site’s heritage and historical record, including its proposed interpretation in the Tÿ Mawr replica museum project in Puerto Madryn, Chubut; and
• recommendations within the Council’s powers, without asking the Council to determine private title, criminal liability or matters reserved to courts or other public bodies.

This is an evidence-review and accountability route. It is not a request for the Council to decide private title or liability.

I am happy to complete the online Scrutiny Topic Suggestion Form if preferred, or to supply any further information the Democratic Services team requires.

Please acknowledge receipt and indicate the process and timescale for consideration.

Kind regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)
Royal Signals Cyber/Electronic Warfare Professional and Life Member

thread: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request
subject: RE: Scrutiny Topic Suggestion / Task and Finish request — Council-held planning, heritage and public-authority record for Great House Farm / Tÿ Mawr, Llandough
body:
Dear Mr Buckler,

Many thanks for your e-mail below and your request for Scrutiny to consider the topic suggested as part of it's Task and Finish work.

Unfortunately, on this occasion we will be unable to consider the request for several reasons:

1. The purpose of Task and Finish is to review existing policy Council considerations and identify areas for future policy direction at a strategic level impacting on a county wide basis. These topics are purposefully strategic in manner, and are based upon areas that Committees determine to have the most positive impact.

2. In addition to the above, the purpose of Scrutiny is not to review evidence related to individual historical decisions and make subsequent recommendations, particularly related to planning, which should be navigated through other channels.

3. We are aware through other correspondence to which you have copied us into that there are ongoing concerns being raised through a variety of channels including Welsh Government, CADW, MSs and MPs, and as such it would not be appropriate for a Scrutiny Task and Finish to add an additional layer of stakeholders and complexity in exploring the issues; notwithstanding points 1 and 2 raised.

Kind Regards,
James

thread: Joint letter to Stephen Doughty MP and Cllr George Carroll
subject: Great House Farm, Llandough
note: No reply from Cllr Carroll appears in the mailbox.
body:
Good Sirs,

I'm writing to you both as elected representatives because, frankly, the
institutional dysfunction I am uncovering is becoming quite extraordinary.

My family — including the last remaining members of my dispossessed Welsh
family in South Wales — have spent 38 years living with the consequences of
what happened to our home and land. They have been frightened into silence,
while the institutions responsible for safeguarding justice, heritage and
public accountability appear, time and again, to have preferred discretion,
obfuscation and exquisitely worded emails to the rather unfashionable
concept of actually answering the questions.

I have now spent considerable time reconstructing what happened. The deeper
I dig, the more the story appears to unravel.

We were not merely separated from a house. We were separated from ancestral
land, family history and heritage. And now the woodland on that land is
being cleared for a development of 133 homes.

One might reasonably ask: *whose history is being developed over, and whose
history is being erased?*

Whatever one's political position, the fact remains that possession being
awarded through historical court proceedings does not magically make every
underlying question of title, evidence, procedure or institutional conduct
disappear. A court order is not an archaeological dig, a title
investigation, or a certificate of immaculate institutional behaviour.

I attach a summary of my grievances concerning CADW, particularly its
historic involvement in this matter. I also attach a mock court application
which I have been developing alongside AI-assisted legal research, not as a
substitute for legal advice, but as a means of stress-testing the evidence
and identifying the questions that require proper legal determination.

I hope you will read them carefully.
This is considerably larger than one parcel of land

The parcel my family occupied — Church View Close — may ultimately prove to
be only one piece of a much larger story.

The same apparent pattern of irregularity that I am investigating in
relation to our parcel appears potentially relevant to:

- the parcel we leased immediately to the east, now proposed for the
133-home development;
- the playing fields subsequently acquired by the council;
- the 33 acres associated with the limeworks; and
- potentially the underlying question of whether the Marquess of Bute
possessed the freehold interest that has subsequently been assumed.

That last question is obviously not something I intend to settle by
rhetorical flourish. It is precisely the sort of question that should be
settled by *documents, title records and evidence*.

One relevant public-record reference is here:

https://www.whatdotheyknow.com/request/2020_01590_hyb

That is the point of my investigation.

I am not asking anybody to accept my conclusions simply because I have
reached them.

*I am asking institutions to produce the evidence.*
What happened to my family cannot simply be filed away

What happened to my family and our home in the 1980s was, in its human
consequences, devastating. From my perspective, it amounted to an assault
on our family itself. And decades of it. At least mid 40's by Western
Ground Rents and onwards.

For decades there has been no meaningful after-support, no meaningful
attempt at reconciliation, no reparative process and, above all, no
satisfactory account of what actually happened.

Instead, the historical record appears fragmented, inaccessible and in
places remarkably difficult to obtain.

CADW is only one of numerous agencies about which my representatives are
now compiling material.

The emerging picture includes questions concerning procedural fairness,
court proceedings, evidential failures, institutional decision-making,
heritage protection and the apparent absence of effective oversight.

The more documents I obtain, the more questions arise.

And I am increasingly uncomfortable with the proposition that *the
descendants of the people affected should have to conduct the investigation
themselves simply to discover what the institutions already ought to know.*

It is particularly distressing that I am having to investigate matters
surrounding my own father's and grandmother's lives and deaths in this way.
I am asking for accountability, not theatre

I appreciate that public bodies have procedures.

I appreciate that officials have workloads.

I appreciate that nobody likes receiving an inconvenient historical file
with several decades' worth of questions attached to it.

But carefully crafted sentences, selective disclosure, unexplained
omissions and silence are not substitutes for accountability.

I have repeatedly encountered what appears to be a culture of concealment,
stealth and institutional defensiveness. Sometimes I receive an answer.
Sometimes I receive an answer to a question I did not ask. Sometimes I
receive an exquisitely polished paragraph which manages, with almost
breathtaking elegance, to avoid answering the actual question.

It is rather like asking for the keys to the filing cabinet and being
handed a brochure about the importance of filing cabinets.

That may be administratively impressive.

It is not an answer.
I am asking you to intervene

I do not expect either of you to determine the merits of my family's
historical or legal claims yourselves.

I am asking you to ensure that the matter receives *proper independent
scrutiny*.

Specifically, I am asking you to assist in ensuring that:

1. relevant surviving records are identified and preserved;
2. agencies holding potentially material records provide substantive
answers rather than procedural evasions;
3. the historical involvement of CADW and other public bodies is
properly examined;
4. the underlying title, conveyancing and land-history evidence is
obtained wherever it survives;
5. any allegations of procedural unfairness or institutional failure are
referred to the appropriate independent bodies where necessary; and
6. my family is finally given a meaningful opportunity to establish,
through evidence, what actually happened.

I have no interest in mythology.

I want the documents.

I want the chronology.

I want the title deeds.

I want the correspondence.

I want the decisions.

I want to know who knew what, when they knew it, what they did with that
information, and why.

If the evidence ultimately disproves some of my suspicions, so be it.

*But the evidence must first be allowed to speak.*
And yes, I am angry

I make no apology for that.

I served this country. I spent years working in public service. I have
worked for the Vale Council. I have served in the military and operated in
circumstances considerably more dangerous than sending an email to a public
authority.

I am therefore perfectly capable of distinguishing between legitimate
administration and institutional stonewalling.

I am no longer asking to be placated.

I am asking for cooperation in recovering whatever evidence remains and
allowing it to be examined properly.

The local community members who have contacted me have long memories. Many
remain convinced that something about this episode was profoundly wrong. I
intend to establish exactly what happened — not through rumour, grievance
or inherited mythology, but through the surviving documentary record.

And if the record contradicts me, I will accept that.

But if the record supports my family, then somebody is eventually going to
have to explain why it took a descendant *38 years, hundreds of enquiries
and an obscene amount of archival digging* to uncover it.

That is not an acceptable model of public accountability.
So, gentlemen — enough of the situationship.

Whatever happened to:

*“We don't negotiate with terrorists”?*

Is there peace?

*No.*

Is there peace?

*No.*

Is there peace?

*No.*

There is, however, apparently an absolutely fabulous quantity of
bureaucracy.

What there has not yet been is accountability.

I therefore ask you, gentlemen, to address this matter with the seriousness
it deserves and to assist my family in obtaining the answers that have been
denied to us for far too long.

I am not asking for special treatment.

I am asking for the truth.

And if the institutions involved have nothing to hide, then surely they
should have nothing to fear from producing the documents.

Regards,

Sion Buckler (Ret'd Sergeant)

thread: Cllr George Carroll (Llandough ward member) — correspondence with no reply
subject: Title Fraud and Procedural Concealment – Church View Close, Llandough (formerly Great House Farm/ "Ty Mawr")
body:
Councillor Carroll & co,

I write regarding potential gaps in the Council's planning and
record-keeping processes relating to Great House Farm, Llandough, which was
demolished in 1988 following the 1987 Court of Appeal decision in BP
Properties Ltd v Buckler.

Recent evidence suggests the Council may wish to examine its own position
on this matter, as it raises questions about procedural compliance and
record integrity that could expose the authority to wider scrutiny.

CORE ISSUES

**1. Identity and Procedural Integrity**

The 1987 judgment turned on a 1974 licence addressed to "Mrs Buckler". My
grandmother, Mary Williams, did not use or accept this designation.
Contemporaneous evidence (1978 newspaper article attached) records her
asserting ownership under her correct name.

If the 1987 court was not presented with this evidence, the judgment may
rest on an incomplete factual record. This raises procedural fairness
concerns relevant to any future review of the decision.

**2. Heritage Information and Statutory Compliance**

The site's archaeological significance was documented by 1978 (Roman
burials, monastic associations). Yet professional excavations in 1994
revealed 1,026 early medieval burials and monastic structures—findings that
should have prompted evaluation under the Ancient Monuments and
Archaeological Areas Act 1979.

Critical question: Did the Council conduct or require prior archaeological
assessment before granting permissions to demolish? If not, this represents
a potential gap in statutory process that may affect the validity of the
permissions granted.

**3. Land Registry Disclosure**

BP registered title in 1982 based on the disputed licence. The Council
should establish:
- Whether any dispute notice or heritage caution was lodged;
- Whether the Council disclosed relevant heritage information to the Land
Registry;
- What planning records exist from 1978–1988 regarding the site's known
archaeological potential.

**4. Corporate Identity Inconsistency**

During my father's appeal, the court treated BP Properties Ltd and BP
Pension Trust Ltd inconsistently—as separate entities when convenient, then
as one when dismissing his claim. This raises questions about how
thoroughly the litigation was scrutinised and whether the Council's records
reflect this uncertainty.

WHY THIS MATTERS TO THE COUNCIL

These issues go beyond a single historical dispute. They touch on:

- **Planning record integrity**: Whether heritage information was
adequately documented and acted upon;
- **Procedural compliance**: Whether statutory protections (Ancient
Monuments Act) were properly applied;
- **Institutional liability**: Whether decisions were made on incomplete or
misleading information;
- **Precedent risk**: Whether similar vulnerabilities may exist in other
historical planning decisions.

REQUESTS

I ask the Council to:

1. **Commission a review** of the planning permissions granted between
1978–1988 for Great House Farm, specifically examining what heritage and
archaeological information was available to decision-makers and how it was
handled.

2. **Refer this matter to the Monitoring Officer** for examination of
procedural compliance and record integrity.

3. **Establish** what correspondence, cautions, or dispute notices exist in
relation to this site's title or heritage status.

4. **Clarify the Council's current protocol** for handling historical title
disputes, previously unknown heritage information, or allegations of
material non-disclosure in past planning processes—to prevent recurrence.

I am not asking the Council to reverse the 1987 judgment or disturb current
residents. I am asking it to ensure its own records are accurate and its
own processes are defensible.

I attach the 1978 article and supporting documents, and am available to
meet or provide further information.

Yours faithfully,

Sion Buckler, Sgt (Ret'd)
Executor for the Manor of Llandough
[redacted]

from almost a decade in the Caribbean in exile protesting this kind of

But it's still an outrage how the Vale of Glamorgan Council treat and

Last year I flew here to the Welsh settlement in Argentina and offered

I truly feel Wales is under a demonic realm spell. It's a hostage/terrorist

I discovered that we weren't "evicted as squatters" after BP vs Buckler

To put it politely. It's taken me swimming through a mud of email lies,

Marconi stayed with us while inventing radio. Peerless Jim fought his first

I am outraged. But more so at the lack of pulse there. Because of the spell
the demonic realm seems to have our people under. Our ancestral land has

citizen/constituent now meaning hostage under terrorist so far as I see.
And those houses, 20 previously at Church View Close and the 133 proposed,
all on my stolen land, which I still own and challenge you all to – are

You cannot consider yourselves an authority without legitimacy. I believe

The community and county and town of Llandough hasn't recognised or

my family there by authorities and community. Until now because of the

falsehoods and even in my already disappointment and outrage at the

As I said this is of a high order. The fraud and concealment is complex. I
did report to fraud teams and within 3 hours they responded refusing to

Multi-generational warfare/lawfare. But it is not limited to our land and

I believe a playbook, even a racket, has been underway in the UK on a
nationwide scale. Problem > reaction > solution. My late nan's inability to

agreement/arrears which amounted to the possession order in the first place

So I'm all too familiar. Because my home in Barry was stolen the same way

I care about me and my family. And how we are treated will be a good

I also say as a certified and experienced commander and leader;

FOI answers. My aim remains straightforward: to understand what happened to

I'm working on plans to rebuild a replica of our 800-year-old former

Here in Puerto Madryn, the full story of the erazure and ongoing supression

https://youtube.com/shorts/-c0UvjM-lwA?is=wvITZl9F2YT8QbuF

With the 133 houses next to the 20 on our stolen occupied land, you will

commander of Akrotiri (with powers of arrest), when I'd take my soldiers on
tour to Nikosia, the UN occupying had to return parcels of land back to
indigenous Greeks or Turks who demanded and got, their ancestral lands
back.

My security group's research so far (50+ soldiers I served with, including
in war) tells me that the definition of "whole farm" in the 1955 court
order did not include our land parcel. The definition had changed from the
1916 agricultural tenancy (two plots) to one plot, i.e., excluding ours,
following a 1928 enactment of an 1877 agreement. The 1955 court’s comment
excluding our parcel by reference to my grandmother Mary Williams’s
"condition and resistance," while omitting any mention of her ownership
claim, looks like an earlier attempt (pre-dating BP’s 1974 reattempt) to

mattered if it were tried in the court it should have been. Having paid

for adverse possession of the parcel by around 1940. The subsequent
multi-generational lawfare appears fundamentally flawed.

The fraud, concealment and suspected government involvement I believe
engage exceptions to the limitation period and justify the case being
reopened. Given the public-interest elements—our home’s associations with
Marconi, Peerless Jim’s first fight there, the large medieval burial site,
the monastery and Roman villa, and the fact that furniture looted during
the eviction originated from Cardiff Castle—I consider a Senedd public
inquiry warranted.

My family remain too fearful to speak openly. The conveniently timed deaths
of our father and grandmother, and the public reporting of us as
"squatters" being evicted (the first time we had been off our land or out
of our home since the 16th century), form part of that context.

Last week South Wales Police already started accepting reports of
casualties like Mamgu, who in fact died of what was a biological weapon.
How much more burying your heads in the sand do you want to get back there?
I'm a military warfare professional, so I pride myself on being difficult
to catch and kill, and on getting to my enemies before they get to me. War
veteran commanders and leaders with full mental and physical health, like
myself, remain on the outskirts of society and upwind for a reason. What
happened to my family is ongoing; be vigilant of it. Learn from it. It was
a manufactured Problem > Reaction > Solution. It was and remains a racket.
Our case is the case to shine light on it because it's so well documented
in the courts and press.

The effort already to drag all this back into the shadows, into more
clandestine/silent and violent warfare, defeats the object here. South
Wales Police want to discuss by phone, not email, after already lying by
saying they hold no records on this. CADW initially lied, albeit they're
cooperating a bit more now. The long-standing council clerk for Llandough
initially declined to engage, before directing me to records on the day his
retirement was announced.

I appreciate you may not have intended “injustice” as a finding of legal
liability, and I do not treat it as such. Having considered what I put
before you, however, you have expressed that you are sure an injustice
occurred. This is the first response I have received from an elected
representative that expressly acknowledges, after consideration of the
material, that an injustice appears to have taken place.

Could you clarify which aspects of the circumstances you were referring to?

I am not asking you to determine legal title. I am asking you to
distinguish between the underlying injustice you recognise and those
particular aspects you consider to lie outside the Council’s remit.

If, for example, you regard the core property dispute as outside the
Council’s jurisdiction, but consider that the Council’s own handling of
planning, heritage, records, FOI requests or constituent concerns remains
within its proper role, I would be grateful if you could identify that
distinction. That would help me understand precisely what you meant and
what, if anything, can properly be addressed through Council channels.

Regards,

Sion
